consensus_summary: Pauline phrase for deeds of obedience to the Mosaic Torah (esp. when treated as basis for justification), contrasted with faith in Christ; dominant readings range over full Torah observance, boundary markers, or ceremonial precepts, with broader extension to general works-righteousness common in Protestant teaching.
book_summary: Deeds performed under obligation imposed by any law or decree (context identifies which); such fulfillment may be obedience but never places the lawgiver in debt or earns benefit.
consensus_core_identification: Observance/deeds required by the Mosaic law as (failed) ground of justification before God.
book_core_identification: Deeds done under obligation of law or decree generally, which cannot put the lawgiver in debt or earn benefit.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus (and its listed alternatives) centers the referent on Mosaic Torah observance in the justification debate; the book detaches the core from that specific corpus and applies the same non-earning principle to any law or decree.
material_contradiction: None; the book explicitly notes the common Mosaic reading and its non-justifying force is compatible with the broadened principle.
rationale: Both identify obligated deeds that fail to justify or create debt. The consensus core remains Mosaic/Pauline; the book keeps that category but materially widens the extension and precision to any law/decree while adding the explicit ‘no debt/earn’ clause. This is boundary refinement (broadening), not replacement of the central idea or a novel referent absent from consensus.
strongest_objection: The printed texts all use ‘works of the law’ in a Mosaic-Torah context; generalizing beyond that corpus may over-extend the phrase’s actual Pauline referent.
